abstract.t: This document defines a TLS 1.3 extension and a structured telemetry record that allow a TLS endpoint to advertise, measure, and export per-handshake post-quantum (PQC) negotiation outcomes. The extension carries values for offered PQC algorithms, the actually negotiated key-exchange suite, and a discrete downgrade-reason code. The associated telemetry record is expressed in CBOR with a CDDL schema, enabling enterprise operators to feed PQC-readiness controllers in a vendor-neutral manner.

The mechanism is intended to fill an observability gap that is not directly addressed by existing TLS 1.3 PQC continuity, downgrade-protection, or hybrid-key-exchange specifications. It provides only the measurement and export surface; concrete scoring weights, thresholds, and rotation triggers are intentionally out of scope and are not disclosed in this Internet-Draft.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Operators migrating production TLS 1.3 fleets to post-quantum (PQC) key exchange require a uniform, vendor-neutral way to observe negotiation outcomes across heterogeneous TLS stacks. Existing specifications focus on detection at the protocol layer; this document focuses on the export and aggregation surface that feeds operational dashboards, SIEM systems, and PQC-readiness controllers.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "MAY" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: TLS Extension: pqc_downgrade_telemetry
section.t: Endpoints MAY include the pqc_downgrade_telemetry extension in ClientHello and EncryptedExtensions. The extension body carries the offered PQC suite identifiers, the negotiated suite identifier, and a one-octet downgrade-reason code. Reason codes are partitioned into peer-incompatibility, policy-override, performance-fallback, and unknown.

section.name: Telemetry Record Schema (CDDL)
section.t: The exported telemetry record is a CBOR map conformant to a CDDL schema defined in Section 5. Required keys include the handshake timestamp, peer identity hint, pqc_offered set, pqc_negotiated value, downgrade_reason code, and an rotation_epoch_id opaque string.

section.name: Operational Considerations
section.t: Operators SHOULD aggregate telemetry across observation windows and SHOULD avoid emitting per-handshake records on high-volume edges; sampled or bucketed export is recommended. This document does not specify scoring weights or alerting thresholds; those decisions are deployment-specific and are not disclosed in this Internet-Draft.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The telemetry surface intentionally exposes only negotiation metadata; it MUST NOT carry handshake secrets, transcript hashes, or private-key material. Operators SHOULD apply transport protection and access controls to telemetry endpoints commensurate with the sensitivity of peer-identity hints.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to register a new TLS ExtensionType value for pqc_downgrade_telemetry from the TLS ExtensionType Values registry, with reference to this document.
